subject: Wrap: PayGrid availability incident — closure notes & operational commitments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Daniels <sophie@paygrid.com>
Cc: PayGrid Ops <ops@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Wrap: PayGrid availability incident — closure notes & operational commitments

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for your patience while our team completed the investigation into the availability impact on Monday. Below is a concise customer-facing closure summary, plus the concrete operational commitments we are delivering to PayGrid. I attached a short visual RCA and a mitigation checklist for your review (filenames below).

Executive summary (2 lines)
- What happened: A misrouted autoscaling signal combined with an edge-cache invalidation spike caused sustained request queuing in the inference routing layer for ~45 minutes.
- Customer impact: Increased latency and 5xxs for a subset of inference traffic (approx. 12% of calls), primarily affecting batch-style transforms between 09:10–09:55 PT.

Root cause (technical)
- A control-plane rollback that restored a previously deprecated autoscaler policy created a transient routing mismatch. That policy cooperated poorly with our new prefix-KV cache invalidation flow, triggering backpressure across a few dedicated GPU pools.

Timeline (high level)
- 09:08 PT — Routine config rollout begins (control-plane).
- 09:10 PT — Cache invalidation job runs (larger shard than usual).
- 09:12–09:57 PT — Elevated queues and 5xx spikes observed; on-call pages.
- 09:34 PT — Temporary mitigation: manual circuit-breaker on affected pools.
- 09:55 PT — Traffic fully routed to fallback pools; normal return.

Immediate fixes delivered
- Disabled the deprecated autoscaler policy and added a hard guard to prevent that policy from being auto-selected.
- Tightened cache invalidation shard sizing and rate-limited invalidations.
- Increased alert thresholds and added a targeted metric to detect queue build-ups earlier.

Customer-facing commitments (owners & dates)
- Engineering: Deploy a routing-policy validation gate to prevent incompatible policy combos — owner: Rishi Malhotra — ETA: 2027-10-09.
- Platform: Auto-heal playbook to move traffic off saturated pools automatically — owner: Marissa Cole — ETA: 2027-10-12.
- Account: One week of service credit (applied to current billing cycle) — owner: Ben Carter — processed by 2027-10-06.
- Comms: Weekly status update for two weeks, tracking the engineering changes and validation tests — owner: Jordan Blake — first update 2027-10-05.

Attachments included:
- paygrid-rca-diagram.png (visual root cause & flow)
- mitigation-checklist.pdf (actions implemented and planned)
- post-incident-timeline.csv (detailed event log)

Next steps / ask of PayGrid
- Can we schedule a 30-minute technical sync next Tuesday (2027-10-05) to walk the validation plan and confirm the rollback guard works for your traffic patterns?
- If you want an expanded on-call contact list or a longer telemetry retention window while we validate, tell us and we will enable it.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Note: I will follow up with the JIRA link for the routing-policy gate and a short recording of the incident timeline walkthrough once we have the engineering notes compiled.

From: Sophie Daniels <sophie@paygrid.com>

Cc: PayGrid Ops <ops@paygrid.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Wrap: PayGrid availability incident — closure notes & operational commitments

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachments. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock next steps:

1) When you say "fallback pools" were used, did any of our traffic hit a lower-performance model variant or different quantization profile? We saw some inference correctness variance on a small sample.
2) For the proposed routing-policy validation gate, will that require any IP allowlist changes on our side or can it be fully handled inside Redwood?

We can do the 10/05 sync — 10:30 PT works for our infra lead. If possible, please include whoever owns the routing-policy change and Marissa for the billing/credit confirmation.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Daniels
Head of Platform Engineering | PayGrid

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Daniels <sophie@paygrid.com>
Cc: PayGrid Ops <ops@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-05T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & 10/05 validation call notes — PayGrid incident wrap

Hi Sophie —

Short update following our 10/05 technical sync — thank you and your infra team for the time. Notes and next commitments below.

What we confirmed on the call
- Fallback routing did not change model variants or quantization profiles; all traffic always executed the same model binary. The observed correctness variance was due to in-flight request retries (duplicate responses arriving during the spike) — we captured the traces and have a remediation to dedupe transient responses.
- The routing-policy validation gate will be implemented entirely in the Redwood control-plane; no IP or config changes required from PayGrid.

Agreed next actions (owners & ETA)
- INF-4521: Implement routing-policy validation gate (Rishi) — complete by 2027-10-09.
- INF-4527: Automatic traffic escape (auto-heal) to bypass saturated pools (Marissa) — staged rollout 2027-10-12; full rollout after validation 2027-10-19.
- INF-4530: Response dedupe and improved request-id tracing to avoid duplicate-correlation artifacts (Engineering) — target 2027-10-15.
- Billing: One week of service credit applied to account on 2027-10-06 (Ben).
- Ops: Extended telemetry retention enabled for PayGrid for 30 days to help validation (Jordan) — enabled now.

Deliverables we uploaded to the shared drive during the call:
- paygrid-rca-diagram.png
- mitigation-checklist.pdf
- post-incident-timeline.csv
- recording: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b-paygrid-incident (video from 10/05)

We will send weekly validation updates on Wednesdays for two weeks starting 2027-10-12. Please let me know if you want a dedicated Slack channel for faster ops coordination; we can provision one scoped to PayGrid infra.

Thanks again —
Jordan
